# WavWiz

> Multi-zone mesh audio wizardry, for gear old and new. One mesh for every speaker you own. Free, MIT-licensed multi-room music system, with no cloud account and no lock-in. Built around Windows, with an optional Linux/Docker server (amd64, plus arm64 for Raspberry Pi since 0.7.0; arm64 not yet verified on real Pi hardware). No telemetry. Public beta.

Current public beta: **0.7.3**, released 27 November 2026. Windows installer: `WavWiz-Setup-0.7.3.exe` (105,079,195 bytes, SHA-256 `4614B9724B4249B926157B1C966B71717E93080A74A784DF5C794B79E62E2B81`). Linux server tarballs: `wavwiz-server-0.7.3-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `wavwiz-server-0.7.3-linux-arm64.tar.gz`. Docker image tags `0.7.3` and `latest` (`docker pull vdubbin74/wavwiz-server:0.7.3`; compose `image: docker.io/vdubbin74/wavwiz-server:0.7.3`). An arm64 image is published; it has not been verified on real Raspberry Pi hardware. New in 0.7.3: Direct (no processing) per speaker (not bit-perfect; that is planned for 0.8.0); a fairer Auto pre-gain so Bass/Treble and boost EQs no longer make the music much quieter, and Loudness really adds bass and treble; Getting started starts with Check your network (Windows) and Public-network guidance; for new setups, phone HTTPS turns on automatically when the server has a home-network address, with a guided per-phone trust step and a list of which phones are secure; clearer HTTPS warnings. 0.7.2 also added live sources in the Windows Player, Announce, and phone drag. Not yet: AirPlay receiver on Linux / Raspberry Pi, and calibration for AirPlay and Cast speakers (both still planned). Planned for 0.8.0: an official Linux Player app (x64 + arm64) that pairs with a WavWiz server and shows up as a zone like the Windows Player; parametric EQ (exact frequency, gain and Q per band) with REW (Room EQ Wizard) filter import; per-speaker room correction using a microphone; convolution/FIR correction file loading; standards-based equal-loudness curves for Loudness; true bit-perfect playback (native sample rate, exclusive output); and DLNA / UPnP renderer output (not available yet). Plans can change; features ship when they're ready.

One mesh for every speaker you own. WavWiz runs a server on an always-on Windows PC (or on Linux, bare or in Docker, on 64-bit Intel/AMD; a 64-bit ARM build for Raspberry Pi 4/5 has been available since 0.7.0 and is not yet verified on real Pi hardware) and plays through Windows WavWiz Players or any modern browser on phones, tablets, Macs, Chromebooks and PCs. The browser uses the device's current system output (built-in speaker, Bluetooth, or HDMI / analog / optical on a Mac, Chromebook or PC, depending on the model); WavWiz does not pick that output in the browser. EQ applies to WavWiz Players only. Bluetooth speakers also work today by pairing them to a Windows PC and choosing that output in the WavWiz Player. An AV receiver can hook up to a Windows Player over HDMI. Zones play different music or link for sync. Each speaker gets its own delay and volume; EQ applies to WavWiz Players. An official Linux and Raspberry Pi Player is planned for 0.8.0, and a DIY guide to revive an old amp with a Pi and a DAC is planned after that player exists. Sources: local folders, NAS shares, internet radio, Subsonic/Navidrome, and (since 0.7.2, in the Windows Player only) that PC's live sound or microphone. Streamers and receivers with AirPlay or Cast can join a zone. AirPlay in from iPhone, iPad and Mac; AirPlay 1 speaker output works; AirPlay 2 output is experimental and off by default. Google Cast output has been available since 0.7.0 and is still in testing. HomePod and Apple TV are unsupported. DLNA / UPnP renderer output is planned for 0.8.0 and is not available yet. AirPlay 1 password speakers, FairPlay, and AirPlay 2 PIN devices are not covered. The Docker image tags 0.7.3 and latest are a multi-arch server (an arm64 image is published): no AirPlay receiver yet, no AirPlay 2 output; since 0.7.0 it can play through the host sound card. Not yet verified on real Raspberry Pi hardware. Calibrate speakers does not support AirPlay or Cast speakers yet. Home Assistant control is via REST plus an optional custom component (not on HACS). Spotify Connect is unofficial, off by default, and needs Premium. AI coding agents wrote the code; the developer designs and tests.
